# Map data sources

`src/lib/geo/indiaMap.ts` is generated by `scripts/build-india-map.mjs` from three public datasets. The app ships the generated file and makes no network calls for the map.

## Attribution the app must show

Show this in small text under the map, with the links clickable where possible:

> Boundaries © [DataMeet India community](https://github.com/datameet/maps) (CC BY 4.0), simplified · PIN locations: Department of Posts, [data.gov.in](https://data.gov.in) (GODL-India) · Places: [GeoNames](https://www.geonames.org) (CC BY 4.0)

Plain-text version:

`Boundaries © DataMeet India community (CC BY 4.0), simplified · PIN locations: Department of Posts, data.gov.in (GODL-India) · Places: GeoNames (CC BY 4.0)`

All three licences allow commercial use and redistribution, including of modified data, as long as attribution is given. We simplified, projected and aggregated the data, which is why the text says "simplified".

## Sources

| Data | Source | Licence | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| State/UT boundaries | DataMeet India community, `States/Admin2.shp` from https://github.com/datameet/maps (the Aug 2021 version, which has Ladakh as a separate UT and the merged Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu) | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The README asks for attribution like: *India boundaries by DataMeet India community (CC BY 4.0)* | `STATE_SHAPES`, `STATE_CENTROIDS`, `VIEWBOX` |
| PIN codes | All India Pincode Directory, Department of Posts, Ministry of Communications, Government of India, published on data.gov.in (https://data.gov.in/dataset/all-india-pincode-directory). Downloaded from the GitHub copy https://github.com/dropdevrahul/pincodes-india (`pincode.csv`: 157,126 rows with data.gov.in's columns, including Latitude/Longitude) | [Government Open Data License – India](https://data.gov.in/government-open-data-license-india) (GODL). Required attribution: the data provider and data.gov.in | `PIN_PREFIX`, `stateFromPincode` |
| Cities | GeoNames `cities1000.txt` (https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/), India rows only | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) | `CITY_COORDS` |
| Towns (place names on site photos) | GeoNames `IN.txt` (same download as Districts), populated places (feature class P) with population ≥ 1,000 plus every district and state headquarters: 7,246 places; built by `scripts/build-places.mjs` into `src/lib/geo/places.ts`, loaded only when the camera opens | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) (credited as "Places: GeoNames") | `PLACES` — nearest town on the photo stamp and towns on its mini map |
| Districts | GeoNames `IN.txt` (https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/IN.zip), feature code ADM2 (763 districts), with `admin1CodesASCII.txt` for state names; built by `scripts/build-districts.mjs` into `src/lib/geo/districts.ts` | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) (already credited as "Places: GeoNames") | `DISTRICTS` — district names on the zoomed-in map |

### Boundary compliance

India requires published maps to show the national boundary as drawn by the Survey of India. The DataMeet `Admin2` layer follows that depiction. We rendered the generated paths and checked them by eye. They include:

- all of Jammu & Kashmir, including the Pakistan-administered areas around Muzaffarabad and Mirpur;
- in Ladakh, Gilgit-Baltistan and Aksai Chin, as on the Survey of India map of November 2019;
- all of Arunachal Pradesh;
- Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep.

Simplification moves lines by about one viewBox unit, roughly 1–3 km. This is a small-scale thematic map. It is not an official Survey of India product, so do not label it as one. If you replace the source, check these areas again.

### How the data was processed

- **Boundaries:**
  - mapshaper (`-simplify interval=1200 keep-shapes`) simplifies the boundaries without opening gaps between neighbouring states.
  - Lakshadweep is the exception: mapshaper merged its islands, so it is taken unsimplified and thinned with Douglas–Peucker at 0.15 units.
  - Paths are projected and then rounded to 0.1 viewBox units.
  - Islands and holes smaller than 0.25 square units (about 2 km²) are dropped. For UTs smaller than 150 square units, every islet bigger than about 0.1 km² is kept, so Chandigarh, Delhi, all four parts of Puducherry, the Lakshadweep islands and Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu all stay visible.
  - Source names are mapped to the names in `src/lib/states.ts`: `Andaman & Nicobar` becomes `Andaman and Nicobar Islands`, and `Jammu & Kashmir` becomes `Jammu and Kashmir`.
- **Projection:** equirectangular, true scale at 23°N, fitted to lat 6–37.5 and lng 68–97.5. The viewBox is 1000 × 1160. The `project()` function in the generated file is the same formula used to draw the paths.
- **Label points:** each `cx/cy` and `STATE_CENTROIDS` entry is the pole of inaccessibility of the state's largest piece. For Puducherry and Lakshadweep we use the piece nearest the capital instead. The point always falls inside the drawn shape.
- **PIN prefixes**, grouped by the first 3 digits:
  - The state is the most common `StateName` in the group.
  - Rows are dropped if their coordinates are missing, unparsable or outside India's bounding box (13.5k of 157k rows). We also drop rows whose coordinates fall outside the office's own state, to remove mis-keyed rows.
  - The location is the median latitude and longitude of the remaining rows.
  - Result: 405 prefixes. 403 use the in-state median. 2 had no in-state points and use the median of all valid rows.
  - These locations are approximate, accurate to the scale of a postal division. Use them for map dots, not for routing.
- **Cities:**
  - Included: every place with population of 3 lakh or more (city sections excluded), plus a hand-picked list of capitals, district headquarters and solar-market towns kept in the script.
  - Where a name is shared, the most populous place wins.
  - Common alternate spellings are added as extra keys.
  - Dharwad and Vasai are not separate places in GeoNames, so their town-centre coordinates are entered by hand in the script.

## Regenerating

You need Node 18 or newer. Network access is needed only to download the source files and mapshaper.

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/geo/states /tmp/geo/pin /tmp/geo/geonames
for e in shp shx dbf prj cpg; do
  curl -sL -o /tmp/geo/states/Admin2.$e https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datameet/maps/master/States/Admin2.$e
done
curl -sL -o /tmp/geo/pin/pincode.csv https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dropdevrahul/pincodes-india/main/pincode.csv
curl -sL -o /tmp/geo/geonames/cities1000.zip https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/cities1000.zip
unzip -o /tmp/geo/geonames/cities1000.zip -d /tmp/geo/geonames

node scripts/build-india-map.mjs \
  --states /tmp/geo/states/Admin2.shp \
  --pins /tmp/geo/pin/pincode.csv \
  --cities /tmp/geo/geonames/cities1000.txt
npx vitest run src/lib/geo
```

Towns for the camera: `node scripts/build-places.mjs <path/to/IN.txt> <path/to/admin1CodesASCII.txt>` (both from https://download.geonames.org/export/dump/), then `npx vitest run src/lib/geo`.

Plus Codes on photos are computed by `src/lib/geo/plusCode.ts`, written from the open [Open Location Code specification](https://github.com/google/open-location-code) and checked against its published test values. No data or service is used for them.

- The script runs `npx --yes mapshaper@0.6.121`. Pass `--mapshaper <path/to/mapshaper>` to use a local copy.
- `--states` also accepts an already simplified GeoJSON with an `ST_NM` property.
- Optional flags: `--out <file>` (default `src/lib/geo/indiaMap.ts`) and `--interval <metres>` (simplification, default 1200). A larger interval gives a smaller file.
- The script warns about cities it cannot find and about city points that fall outside every shape. It throws if a canonical state is missing from the source.
- Keep the generated file under about 250 KB. It is currently about 222 KB.
- A newer source file may change the generated file and the PIN medians a little. Review the diff and re-run the tests.
